selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What question is asked at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: It asks whether all created things say “In the Name of Allah” in the way they are made and the way they act.

questions.question: What everyday-style example is used to help explain that statement?
questions.answer: An example is given of one man making a whole town’s people gather and work.

questions.question: After this example, what big truth does the passage teach about all things?
questions.answer: It teaches that all things work under Allah’s authority.

questions.question: How are gardens described in a way that helps us understand their blessings?
questions.answer: They are described like cooking places where many kinds of foods are prepared for people.

questions.question: How are gardens like places where food is prepared?
questions.answer: They bring forth many different foods as if meals are being made for us.

questions.question: What surprising thing do soft roots do?
questions.answer: They go through hard soil and even rock.

questions.question: What unusual ability do roots and rootlets have?
questions.answer: They can enter and pass through very hard ground and stone.

questions.question: Who is criticized in the passage for trusting only in nature and physical causes?
questions.answer: People who explain things as if nature works by itself are criticized.

questions.question: How do the examples of roots and leaves answer people who only trust natural causes?
questions.answer: They show that the real control belongs to Allah, not to blind natural forces.

questions.question: What claim from earlier is being checked again at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: The claim is that all beings say “In the Name of Allah” through how they are created and how they behave.

questions.question: What would you conclude if one person controlled a whole town by force?
questions.answer: I would conclude that he has authority and support from a ruler.

questions.question: If that person is really able to do it, whose support must he have?
questions.answer: He must have support from a ruler or government.

questions.question: Why are seeds and grains mentioned before trees?
questions.answer: They show how something very small can be the beginning of something much bigger.

questions.question: What does the passage say trees do for us?
questions.answer: They bring out blessings and offer useful things like fruits and produce.

questions.question: Why are cows, camels, sheep, and goats called blessed in this passage?
questions.answer: Because Allah gives people great benefit through them, especially milk.

questions.question: Why is the milk compared to something life-giving?
questions.answer: Because it is pure, beneficial, and a precious nourishment.

questions.question: What does that surprise help us understand?
questions.answer: It helps us understand that physical weakness does not stop what Allah commands.

questions.question: What two examples from prophets are used near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: One example is Musa striking the rock, and the other is Ibrahim being safe from fire.

questions.question: What wrong idea is being pushed back against by these examples?
questions.answer: The idea that nature or material causes are in charge by themselves is being pushed back against.

questions.question: What is the main question raised in the first line of the target passage?
questions.answer: It asks whether all things really declare Allah’s name by the way they function.

questions.question: Is the answer doubtful or certain in the passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as certain.

questions.question: Why would a single person ordering around a whole town seem impossible by his own strength?
questions.answer: Because one person alone would not have enough power or authority to do that.

questions.question: What is surprising about the roots of plants and trees?
questions.answer: Even though they are very soft, they can move through hard ground and rock.

questions.question: What teaching is asked about in the first sentence of the target passage?
questions.answer: It asks whether all beings really proclaim Allah’s name by their very state.
